The microstructure of the as-deposited superalloys consists of few topological close packet (TCP) phases distributed between g-Ni dendrites with epitaxial growth characteristic.
The formation TCP phases mostly results from micro-segregations of alloying elements (especially elements of high atomic, such as niobium, molybdenum, etc.) during LAM process

evidence.quote: The microstructure of the as-deposited superalloys consists of few TCP phases distributed between g-Ni dendrites with epitaxial growth characteristic. With the increase of Cr-like elements amount, TCP phases change from granular Laves to long-striped Laves plus acicular s, and exhibit a trend of first decreasing and then increasing in amount, with the lowest value obtained in NiCrlike-2 alloy.
The microstructure of the as-deposited superalloys consists of few TCP phases distributed between g-Ni dendrites with epitaxial growth characteristic.
microhardness values slightly increase with the increase of Cr-like elements amount
hardness and yield strength of as-deposited alloys increase with the increase of Cr-like elements with larger atomic radius
The formation TCP phases mostly results from micro-segregations of alloying elements (especially elements of high atomic, such as niobium, molybdenum, etc.) during LAM process

In the case of the alloys with higher level of Cr-like elements, Cr2O3, which grows in the form of network along the grain boundaries, arises first through "selective oxidation", and then a mixed external scale of spinels NiFe 2O4 and NiCr2O4 is formed in the dendritic area.
This implies that NiCr2O4 scale has a weaker adhesion to substrate and easily spalls away during oxidation process, which causes an internal oxidation to form thin NiO scale.

It has been generally accepted that solidification cracking was caused by the separation of residual liquid under tensile stress at last stage of solidification, and characterized by extended openings that formed during solidification in the mushy zone, where the liquid feeding was difficult and the transverse shear strength of the material was very low.
It has been recognized that liquation cracking results from liquation of low melting point eutectic at grain boundary and the tensile stress.
